newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to talk a bit longer about alcohol fuel.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to talk a bit longer about alcohol fuel.

text.p: The Brazilian government will set up an interministerial group in the next few days to find ways of encouraging the use of alcohol as a vehicle fuel, officials said Wednesday.

Another working group will evaluate existing proposals such as the introduction of a "green" tax on petroleum fuels and incentives for taxi drivers, car hire companies and government offices to use alcohol-powered cars, they said.
"We've been discussng this subject for a year and a half and now we'll talk about the best way of doing it," said Frederico Alvarez, executive secretary of Brazil's Foreign Trade Chamber.
Upcoming discussions would also include representatives of carmakers operating in Brazil, he said.
Until recently, alcohol was commonly used as a car fuel in Brazil, a locally produced alternative to imported petroleum. But shortages after bad harvests and other problems led to a sharp slump.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso raised the prospect of a renaissance in alcohol fuel as a solution to the world's pollution problems at this week's Earth Summit at the United Nations.
